chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from Muhammad ibn Hammam, from Ubaydullah ibn al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammoon, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, saying:

We were gathered by our father Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, and he said: "O my sons, beware of meddling with the rights of others, and be patient when visited by misfortune. And if some of your people call you to a matter whose harm to you is greater than its benefit for you, then do not respond to them."
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad, the Prophet, and his pure progeny.

key_terms.إياكم: Beware -- a strong Arabic warning formula
key_terms.التعرض للحقوق: Meddling with the rights of others -- encroaching on what is owed to people
key_terms.النوائب: Misfortunes/calamities -- trials that befall a person

ai.seo_question: What advice did Imam al-Baqir give his sons about rights, patience, and harmful requests?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) recounts that his father Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) gathered his sons and gave them three pieces of advice: do not encroach upon the rights of others, endure hardships patiently, and refuse any invitation from your kinsmen whose harm outweighs its benefit. This was guidance given to the Imam's own household, reflecting the practical wisdom the Ahl al-Bayt taught their families in Medina during the early 2nd century AH.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 11. He said: Abul Qasim Ja’far ibn Muhammad, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from Muhammad ibn Hammam, from Abdullah ibn al-Ala’, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammoon, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, say:

We were gathered together by (our father) Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, and then he said: "O my sons, beware of meddling with the rights of others, and be enduring when visited by any misfortune, and if people call you to any matter whose harm to you is more than its benefit, do not respond."
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad, the Prophet and his pure progeny.
